sentences.show: In 1937, the most famous pilot in the world vanished over the Pacific. 89 years later, we are still looking for her.
Amelia Earhart. The first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic.
In 1937, she set out to fly around the world, with her navigator, Fred Noonan.
22,000 miles done. 7,000 to go, almost all of it ocean.
On 2 July, they took off from New Guinea for Howland Island. A strip of land two kilometres long, in the middle of the Pacific.
A Coast Guard ship, the Itasca, waited there to guide them in by radio.
The ship could hear her loud and clear. But she could not hear the ship.
Her last calls said they were running low on fuel, and could not find the island.
The Navy searched for over two weeks. Ships, seaplanes, an aircraft carrier. $4 million. Nothing.
Did they crash into the sea? Die as castaways on a remote island? Or were they captured by the Japanese?
In 2017, a photo seemed to show them alive in Japanese hands. Then it turned up in a book from 1935. Two years before they vanished.
And this October, an expedition to Nikumaroro Island checked a shape under the water that might have been her plane. It was a clump of trees.
Amelia never found her island. You can still find the subscribe button.
